title_candidates: Google adds faster Gemini image and video models
summary: Google released Nano Banana 2 Lite for faster image generation and Gemini Omni Flash for video generation and conversational editing across AI Studio, the Gemini API, and consumer surfaces.

primary_source.title: Start building with Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash
primary_source.author: Google DeepMind
key_facts: Google released Nano Banana 2 Lite as its fastest and most cost-efficient Gemini image model in the Nano Banana family.
Nano Banana 2 Lite is available in Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and is rolling out to consumer surfaces.
Google says Nano Banana 2 Lite produces text-to-image outputs in about four seconds and costs $0.034 per 1K-resolution image.
Google also made Gemini Omni Flash available for developers through Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, and the enterprise platform.
Gemini Omni Flash supports video generation and conversational editing from text, image, and video inputs.

steps.instruction: Open Google AI Studio and look for Nano Banana 2 Lite or Gemini image/video model options.
Start with a harmless image prompt, such as a product moodboard or classroom poster draft.
Check whether the output has readable text, consistent characters, and no unexpected brand or person likeness.
If Omni Flash is available in your account, try one short video-editing request using non-private footage.
Save the prompt and result so you can compare quality, latency, and cost before using it in a repeated workflow.
